title: Sustainable City Building Programme (SCBP) for Decentralized Sanitation in Indian Cities
background: Indian cities, especially rapidly growing urban areas and peripheries, face significant challenges with inadequate urban sanitation systems. Traditional centralized systems are often unviable in these areas, necessitating decentralized (non-networked) sanitation solutions to ensure sustainable and equitable access to sanitation services.
problem: Inadequate urban sanitation systems in Indian cities, particularly in rapidly growing urban areas and peripheries, requiring decentralized (non-networked) sanitation solutions.
solution: The Sustainable City Building Programme (SCBP) engages academic institutions through a structured program that integrates non-networked sanitation into curricula, research, and training. This includes Round Table meetings, faculty training workshops, and Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) with universities. Additionally, SCBP develops modular educational content, workshops, and research projects to foster interdisciplinary approaches to decentralized sanitation systems.
technology_used: Participant Kit (modular educational toolkit for water and sanitation)
department: Academic Institutions and Urban Development Authorities
competencies_required: Skills in designing decentralized sanitation solutions
key_outcomes: 9 universities signed MOUs with SCBP by March 2019
Training of over 500 students and professionals
Initiation of state-level workshops in Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu
Facilitation of collaborative problem-solving at CEPT University through sandpit activities and distribution of certificates
lessons_learned: The critical role of academic-industry partnerships in scaling decentralized sanitation solutions
The need for modular and adaptable educational tools to address diverse urban contexts
